decisions.quote:
We attempted to replicate a brief social–psychological inter-
vention reported in Cohen et al. (2006) that has been replicated

decisions.location: Results and Discussion, Analytical replication, p. 5
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row (input_row_index 1059) and blind target 0 identify Cohen, Garcia, Apfel, & Master (2006), 'Reducing the Racial Achievement Gap: A Social-Psychological Intervention' (Science, 313, 1307-1310; DOI 10.1126/science.1128317), specifically Study 1, as the original study directly replicated in two new school samples.

decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code the replication outcome for Cohen et al. (2006) as 'failed'. Across ANOVA, the exact analytical replication regression model (Table 1), multilevel models, and time-series analyses in both schools, the self-affirmation intervention had no statistically significant effect on overall or Black/Hispanic student GPA, and the authors explicitly characterize the result as a failure to replicate the original effect.

decisions.quote:
We attempted to replicate a self-affirmation intervention that produced a 40% reduction in the academic achievement gap among
at-risk students. The intervention was designed as a protection against stereotype threat—, which creates stress and suppresses
the performance, engagement, and learning of students stereotyped as intellectually inferior. In previous research, Black and
Hispanic students who engaged in a values-affirmation exercise significantly improved their academic performance over the
course of a school semester. We attempted to replicate these salutary effects in both an inner-city school and a more wealthy
suburban school—contexts not tested in the original research. Despite employing the same materials, we found no effect of the
affirmation on academic performance.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind agree the record type is 'replication'. The authors collected new experimental data in two ninth-grade school samples using the original materials from Cohen et al. (2006) to re-test whether the self-affirmation intervention improves academic performance.
